Biophysical characterization

Size, charge and stability: the developability readouts that decide which candidate moves forward.

Assays
3
Standard turnaround
3–6 days
Fastest priority slot
2 days

Biophysical assays are where candidate selection usually happens. We run aggregation, thermal stability and charge-variant panels side by side so you can compare molecules on the same day, on the same instruments, with the same analyst.

Panels can be run on as little as a few hundred micrograms per candidate, which makes them practical early in discovery when material is scarce.

Questions this answers

  • How much high-molecular-weight species is present?
  • Where does each candidate unfold, and does it aggregate on the way?
  • How many charge variants are there, and do they change under stress?
  • Which formulation buffer holds up best?

Sample requirements

Sample requirements for biophysical characterization
Minimum amount300 µg per candidate for the full panel
Concentration1 mg/mL or higher
BufferSend a matching buffer blank, at least 5 mL
Shipping2–8 °C, or frozen if the molecule tolerates freeze–thaw

What you receive

  • Side-by-side candidate comparison table
  • Chromatograms, melting curves and electropherograms
  • Analyst notes on anything unusual
  • Raw data and processing parameters
